svg.text: AU Bank Insurance Distribution Platform — North Star High-Level Design
Bank as IRDAI Corporate Agent / Composite Corporate Agent · Life · Health · General/Motor · assisted, DIY, hybrid, call-centre and certified-SP journeys · AWS ap-south-1
Target state and the release path to it. The seams exist from R0; the capabilities arrive by release.
READ THIS FIRST — THIS IS A TARGET-STATE DIAGRAM, NOT ADMITTED SCOPE

Only the R0 band is inside WS-3 current_scope in docs/governance/state/CURRENT-STATE.yaml. Every R1–RN element is either an out_of_scope item with a revisit_at, or not yet triaged at all. This diagram is an architecture intent artefact: it exists so that R0 is built with the right seams — it is not a licence to build R1+ now.
RELEASE COLOUR MODEL — LIFE FIRST, THEN HEALTH, THEN GENERAL/MOTOR

The chip on every element below is the release in which that element FIRST EXISTS.
LINE OF BUSINESS (LB-4 / LB-5) — which boxes get a second copy when Health arrives:
shared code, ONE deployment — behaviour resolved from configuration keyed by (lob, …), never forked ·
inside a rose LOB cell — Health and General each get their OWN instance; Quote and Proposal are frozen here ·
untagged and outside every cell — one instance for every line of business, forever (party, lead, consent, payment, policy, audit).
THE JOURNEY SPINE — the object model every boundary below is organised around
R2 · Policy renewal due, expiry or lapse creates a NEW Lead and a NEW Journey — an existing journey is never reopened
Cardinality — get this wrong and everything else bends around it
Party 1:N Lead · Lead 1:N Journey · Journey 1:1 Policy on success · Policy 1:N follow-on Lead.
partyId ≠ bankCustomerId ≠ leadId ≠ journeyId. A prospect exists with no CIF and is linked to one later without disturbing the journey.
Enforced rule instead of a hard 1:1: only one ACTIVE journey per Party + LOB + product context.
BANK owns: party, lead, suitability, consent, product selection, proposal capture, payment, policy record, servicing intent.
INSURER owns: risk and medical assessment, underwriting decision, loading, exclusion, counter-offer, decline, and the policy contract.
We track insurer status, requirements and next action. We never compute a risk decision.
Actors are JourneyParticipants, not owners: customer, RM (the certified SP), insurance partner rep, branch, call-centre agent and operations act on the SAME journey.
Every action carries an InteractionContext (actor, type, channel, device, session, branch, correlationId) — that is what makes the timeline and audit answerable.
What an actor may do is decided by the PDP from role + certification + branch + LOB + stage, never by hiding a button.
who does the work, and where
OWNS · Every human and system that starts or continues a journey.

DOES NOT OWN · Journey state, business rules or LOB knowledge. A journey is never owned by a channel — actors are participants on one journey (JourneyParticipant), so a customer can start on the web, be helped by the call centre and be closed by an RM without a second journey being created.
Bank RM — the certified Specified Person

scope, validity), not an actor — checked per action.

after the RM completes need analysis + suitability.

Lead and reuse the same journey.
No new business architecture per channel.
EDGE — THE ONLY PUBLIC ENTRY POINT
OWNS · Public exposure, TLS termination, WAF, CDN, rate limiting and north-south routing.

DOES NOT OWN · Business logic or authorization decisions. Every service and every data store sits in a private subnet; if Nginx is used at all it is private behind the internal ALB — never an EC2 with a public IP.
Public DNS for the bank's insurance
custom iRules, bot control at edge.
OWNS · Channel-shaped aggregation, session and token custody, screen-oriented composition.

DOES NOT OWN · Domain rules, journey state or provider vocabulary. One BFF per channel — never one BFF per channel × LOB. There is no RM-Life-Quote-Service: RM, customer and call centre all call the same Life Quote.

SHARED PLATFORM PLANE — BUILT ONCE FOR EVERY LOB

OWNS · Concepts that mean the same thing whichever line of business is being sold: who the customer is, why we are contacting them, what we are permitted to do, where they are, what they paid and what they hold.

DOES NOT OWN · How a specific insurance product is quoted, proposed or underwritten. There is no life-customer-service / health-customer-service / general-consent-service — duplicating these per LOB is the failure mode this plane exists to prevent.

and SP identities at R2. Two identity domains,

RULE — a capability belongs here only if the business concept is fundamentally the same for Life, Health and Motor. If the behaviour, traffic profile or change rate genuinely differs by LOB, it belongs in a cell below.

Journey Registry resolves the LOB and routes to the owning cell. Public routes stay resource-shaped — /journeys/{id}/quotes, /journeys/{id}/proposal — never /life/quote. The router is the only place that knows the LOB→cell map, so adding Health at R3 and General at R4 is a configuration and deployment change, not a redesign.
single-LOB pass-through at R0 → real router at R1
LOB EXECUTION CELL PLANE — WHERE THE INSURANCE BUSINESS ACTUALLY DIFFERS

OWNS · A cell is an independently deployable, scalable, observable, configurable, versionable, releasable and failure-isolated execution boundary — not one service and not one container. Quote and Proposal are per-LOB and that boundary is frozen: a Life quote, a Health quote and a Motor quote do not share a field shape, so sharing a service produces exactly the if (lob == …) sprawl this design exists to prevent.

DOES NOT OWN · Customer, consent, product governance, payment, policy registry, documents, notification or audit — those are shared above. Nor the underwriting decision: that is the insurer's. A failed Life release must never make Health or Motor unavailable, and an insurer timeout storm in Life must never consume Health's capacity.

age · sum assured · term · premium frequency · smoker · riders.

Deciding this early would be premature; making it impossible would be the real error.

SHARE THE FRAMEWORK, NOT THE RUNTIME · canonical contracts · Quote/Proposal SDK · adapter framework · observability library · error model · idempotency helpers · security libraries — all shared as versioned libraries and standards, while the deployables, databases, caches, queues and connection pools stay isolated per cell.
bank-canonical request — the cell never speaks provider

OWNS · Receive a bank-canonical insurance request, decide where it must go, fan out where necessary, translate to provider formats, manage provider communication and return a canonical bank response. Routing, adapters, transformation, provider auth, resilience, callbacks, provider reference mapping, idempotency, error normalization, provider observability.

DOES NOT OWN · Journey state, suitability, which product should be recommended, consent, or the insurer's underwriting decision. Two orchestrations must never merge: business journey orchestration answers 'what happens next for this customer', provider orchestration answers 'which provider gets this call and how'.

EVOLUTION — R0: one shared Integration Hub, 1SB only. R1–R2: control plane (standards, registry, credentials, resilience) separated from runtime. R3–R4: runtime partitioned per LOB so no LOB queues behind another. RN: the bank's own aggregation platform, direct and aggregator routes side by side, switchable per product and per operation by configuration.
EXTERNAL BOUNDARIES — BANK SYSTEMS vs INSURANCE PROVIDERS

OWNS · Two separate integration boundaries, deliberately. Bank-system integration (CBS, CRM, PG, AD) is isolated from insurance-provider integration so a core-banking change never leaks into Life Quote, and an insurer change never touches customer lookup.

DOES NOT OWN · Anything canonical. Provider and bank vocabulary terminates inside its adapter package. Outbound provider traffic leaves through controlled egress — NAT gateway with a stable Elastic IP the insurer can allowlist, or VPN / Direct Connect / private connectivity with mTLS.

THE DASHED GREY BAND IS NOT SCOPE. These are integrations a mature platform will eventually need, drawn so the gap is visible rather than forgotten. None has a triage record, an ADR or an owner today; each must go through the AIGEM pipeline before it becomes work.

OWNS · Durable state, evidence and documents. Database ownership per bounded context is mandatory and cross-service database access is forbidden (ArchUnit + IAM). Physical separation is workload-driven, not dogmatic.

DOES NOT OWN · Shared mutable tables. 'Database per service' does not mean forty Aurora clusters across three environments plus DR — that is a cost, upgrade, backup and DBA problem, not an architecture. DECIDED (ADR-008): start with schema separation in ONE cluster; split when scale, blast radius, security or RTO justify it, and split along the LOB-cell / shared-platform seam rather than the service boundary.

WHAT LANDS WHEN — release strategy follows business maturity, not architecture completeness

We are not building Life, Health and Motor now. R0 proves Life; R1 and R2 mature Life; R3 introduces Health; R4 introduces General/Motor. The architectural seams exist from R0 so that adding Health later does not require redesigning Life — that is the entire point of drawing the target now.

one ETB customer of one Group A insurer, end to end.

PERMANENT — TRUE IN R0 AND STILL TRUE IN RN. Breaking one of these is a redesign, not a change.
One Lead may have many Journeys. Renewal and lapse create a NEW Lead and a NEW Journey — an old journey is never reopened. Opportunity is the durable-demand alias only.
A journey is never owned by a channel

RM (the certified SP), insurance partner rep, customer and call centre are participants on one journey. A certification is an attribute on a participant, never a participant of its own. No RM-Life-Quote-Service and no per-channel journey type.
No cross-LOB failure propagation by design. A failed Life release, or an insurer timeout storm in Life, must not affect Health or Motor.
Quote and Proposal are per-LOB — frozen
Life, Health and Motor quote and proposal field shapes are genuinely different. Sharing the service produces the if (lob == …) sprawl we are avoiding.
The bank owns suitability, product selection and the distribution journey. We track insurer status, requirements and next action; we never decide risk.
1SB is a provider route, not a domain dependency
Provider vocabulary terminates in adapter.<provider>.*. No bank service calls an adapter directly; provider traffic goes through the aggregation layer.
Never one giant InsuranceRequest. A provider identifier is never a bank primary key; a 1SB jobId is never a caller handle.
Consent is evidence, not a boolean
No quote without a valid, unexpired suitability assessment. No proposal without an unexpired consent grant. Both are append-only and immutable.
Premium payment executes only on the customer's own device. A policy is never issued against a payment that is not RECONCILED.
Insurer-per-class limits, product matrices, channel enablement, ETB/NTB and provider routes are versioned config under maker-checker — never code.
Every significant business action emits an event; audit is append-only WORM for 7 years in India regions. Audit is not logging.
One public entry point at the edge. No application, database or cache is internet-reachable; provider egress is controlled and allowlistable.
Own the data, be pragmatic about the cluster
Database ownership per bounded context is mandatory and cross-service DB access is forbidden. Physical splitting is driven by scale, security and RTO, and follows the LOB seam (ADR-008).
General/Motor is modelled so Motor can become its own cell later without rewriting the platform. Build the seam; defer the split.

AI-DRAFTED in the Architecture lane (Mahesh — Board 1, Principal Insurance Platform Architect). Mandatory human T4 Architecture sign-off is OUTSTANDING; this diagram approves nothing and admits nothing.

Reading rule · The R0 band is the executable architecture and the only admitted scope. R1–R4 elements correspond to CURRENT-STATE out_of_scope entries and carry that entry's revisit_at. RN elements have no governance record at all. Nothing on this diagram may be cited as authority to start work: each element still requires AIGEM triage, an owner, and where consequential an ADR and the applicable board reviews.

Companion artefacts · docs/architecture/r0-reference-architecture.svg is the R0 executable HLD. · Revised 2026-08-25 — CR-013 / ADR-014: spoken name of #5 is Lead; #18 Reporting & MIS and the #19 admin UI are R0 on the isolated read path; campaign/bulk Lead create stays R1. Human T4 outstanding. OPEN-D10 closed as Lead (Opportunity remains the durable-demand alias).
